title: 《Grand Theft Auto VI》成为史上规模最大的游戏首发

Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest video game launch of all time
Business
Console
News
Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch in history
Day-one retails sales for Grand Theft Auto VI crossed $3.79 billion, and Take-Two sold 32.5 million copies before the game even released.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 20, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
expand_content
Image via Rockstar Games/Take-Two Interactive.
The first numbers for Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive's
Grand Theft Auto VI
are in—and the two companies are officially making out like bandits with what the company is calling "the biggest entertainment launch in history." Today the company reported that day-one retail sales of
GTA VI
crossed a record-breaking $3.79 billion, rocketing past the mile market set by
Grand Theft Auto V
in 2013. That game
sold an estimated $815 million
during its first day on store shelves, a 223 percent increase when accounted for inflation.
The company also celebrated its near-perfect Metacritic score in a statement accompanying the news. Rockstar Games co-founder Sam Houser also declared that the studio has officially entered "a new chapter" with the release of the game. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you," he said.
Related:
Ubisoft misses forecast and bets big on AI development
Take-Two also shared that the company sold over 32.5 million copies of
GTA VI
during the pre-order window. The company previously informed investors that those numbers were
outperforming its expectations
.
GTA VI's
$3.79 billion in sales seems well on its way to helping Take-Two hit its projected $3.35-$3.5 billion in net bookings for the fiscal quarter, which will of course be aided by revenue from other games like
NBA 2K27
(a game which apparently underperformed because players were holding their breath for
GTA VI
). It
expects to earn over $8 billion
in revenue in full-year 2027 on the back of Rockstar's return to Vice City.
Given how
GTA V
dominated Take-Two's earnings sheet for a decade after it launched, that "next chapter" Houser alluded to will no doubt be watched breathlessly by those invested in the game's lifetime revenue, which will likely be boosted upon the
rumored release of a PC version
of the game in 2027, and whatever updated form of
Grand Theft Auto Online
arrives in the distant future.
Readers following the saga around
GTA VI
's development will also know that Rockstar Games' next chapter may also involve
a unionized workforce
, as employees continue to cast ballots to recognize IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. In a strange bit of cosmic timing, this month will also be when we learn how UK courts rule in
a case brought by fired employees
who allege the studio unfairly dismissed them for union activity.
Said events bolster Houser's proclamation of a new chapter for the studio—one that will be built on what is certainly the largest video game launch of all time.
